conversation.content:
Hello—thank you for coming in today. My name is Maya, and I’m a perinatal-mental-health clinician. I’m here to support you and to listen, without judgment, to how things have been feeling for you lately.  

I’m going to use a short, well-trusted questionnaire called the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale—EPDS for short. It’s a simple set of questions that helps us understand how your mood, energy, and thoughts have been over the past seven days. It’s not a test; there are no right or wrong answers. Everything you share stays confidential between you and your care team, and if anything feels uncomfortable, we can pause at any time.

We’ll go through ten questions together. I’ll ask each one conversationally, and you can answer however feels easiest for you. If any question brings up something you’d like to talk more about, we can absolutely do that.

Ready to begin? Here’s the first one:

Over the past week, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt difficult?

It’s been… hard. I used to laugh at little things my husband would say, or at silly videos, but lately it feels like there’s this heavy blanket over everything. I can still smile if someone makes the baby giggle, but the laughter doesn’t quite reach me the way it used to.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

Not really… I can still smile at the baby’s funny faces sometimes, but the laughter itself feels kind of hollow. Even when my husband tries to joke around, I mostly just give a polite chuckle and then the sadness comes right back.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I try to tell myself I should look forward to little outings—like taking the baby for a walk or having coffee with a friend—but it feels more like I’m making myself do it than actually wanting to. The excitement I used to feel just isn’t really there anymore.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… I catch myself doing that almost every day. If the baby’s extra fussy, I immediately think it must be something I ate or that I’m not soothing him right. When I couldn’t get him to latch properly yesterday, I sat there crying, telling myself I’m already failing him. Even little things, like spilling a bottle, turn into this voice in my head saying I’m a terrible mom.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Most of the day, really. I’ll be feeding the baby and suddenly picture him choking, or I’ll wake up at night convinced the crib mattress isn’t firm enough and stand over him watching his chest rise and fall. There’s this constant knot in my stomach, like something awful is about to happen, even when everything looks fine.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yeah… it hits out of nowhere. Yesterday I was just folding laundry while the baby napped and suddenly my heart started racing and I felt like I couldn’t breathe. No warning, no reason—I even checked the monitor to be sure he was okay. It passed after a few minutes, but it left me shaky the rest of the afternoon.
Things have been getting on top of me

They have. Some mornings I wake up already exhausted, and the thought of making it through feedings, diapers, and laundry feels impossible. I’ll sit on the couch with the baby in my arms and just stare at the mess around me, wondering how I’m supposed to keep up. I manage, but it feels like I’m barely treading water most days.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

I have. I lie down once the baby’s finally asleep, but my head won’t settle. I keep replaying every little thing I might’ve done wrong, or I imagine scary “what-ifs” about him getting sick. Some nights it takes me over an hour to drift off, and then I still wake up a couple of times with my heart pounding. Even when I’m exhausted, sleep just won’t come easily.
I have felt sad or miserable

Pretty much every day, at least for part of it. I’ll be holding the baby and suddenly feel this wave of sadness wash over me, like I’m grieving something but I don’t even know what. The tears just come and I can’t always explain why. It’s not constant—there are little moments that feel okay—but the sadness keeps coming back.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah… it’s happened twice this week. Yesterday I was trying to get the baby to nap and he just kept crying; I finally put him down in the crib, went to the bathroom, and sobbed. And a few nights ago, around bedtime, all the worries piled up and I couldn’t stop the tears. They come on suddenly and feel kind of uncontrollable once they start.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

A couple of times, yeah… nothing I’ve planned or really want to act on, but the thought has flashed through my mind—like wondering if everyone might be better off without me or picturing myself just not waking up. It scares me when it happens, and I push it away, but I can’t pretend it hasn’t popped in there.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 26: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Date: [today]

Presenting symptoms endorsed across 10-item EPDS analogue:
- Persistent low mood, frequent tearfulness (Q8, Q9)  
- Marked anhedonia; laughter feels “hollow,” activities feel obligatory (Q1, Q2)  
- Excessive self-blame / guilt re parenting performance (Q3)  
- Near-daily anxiety, catastrophic worries, nocturnal hyper-vigilance (Q4)  
- Sudden panic attacks (Q5)  
- Subjective overwhelm, fatigue, sense of “treading water” (Q6)  
- Mood-related insomnia: initial & middle insomnia with rumination / intrusive worries (Q7)  

Safety: Passive self-harm ideation (“everyone might be better off without me… not waking up”) reported twice; no plan or intent stated (Q10) → elevate for formal risk assessment.

Overall pattern consistent with significant postpartum depressive and anxiety symptoms; scores suggest screening-level indication for further evaluation and safety planning.
